headline: Dry through Friday apart from a weak Thursday system; a possible weak weekend system is a toss-up in track and timing.
summary: As of Tuesday evening, forecasters expect tonight and Wednesday to stay dry, with Wednesday warmer than normal for October. Light winds tonight could let patchy fog form early Wednesday in sheltered spots, but it should lift and break up by late morning. A weak system brushes the area Thursday, bringing more clouds and near-normal temperatures. Models show only a few very limited, short-lived showers, mainly in the Olympics and north Cascades Thursday afternoon and evening. Friday looks dry with near-normal temperatures. The weekend is much less certain. A weak system may arrive Saturday night into Sunday, but the computer models are nearly split on its path. Some show a more direct, somewhat more organized but likely still weak system. Others show a slower or more northerly track, or one staying offshore, which would mean less rain or pushing it to Sunday or even Monday. Early next week is also close to a coin flip, at 49% for high pressure (drier) versus 51% for a trough (cooler, unsettled). Confidence is high for the next couple of days and for Thursday's system being weak. No hazards are expected.
changes: The early-morning discussion expected rain likely Saturday night into Sunday morning and a possibly record-cold Monday morning. By evening, the weekend system was described as weak and uncertain, with rain possibly delayed to Sunday or Monday, and the cold Monday mention was gone.
